subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs make persisted session defaults intentional, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because an older session value can shadow later operator policy changes.

options.title: Clamp sessions to operator policy
options.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the upper bound and clear, clamp, or migrate stored session fields that exceed it, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep current session contract
options.body: Document that `/exec` session defaults can outlive config changes and that operators must reset sessions or use a repair flow to enforce new policy on existing lanes.

options.title: Add reset or doctor first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair path before changing precedence for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Clamp sessions to operator policy
recommendation.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the upper bound and clear, clamp, or migrate stored session fields that exceed it, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the `/exec` session override behavior and focused precedence tests points to this owner path.
